result.scope: Isolated inspection of adapter port construction with the kernel factory replaced by identity. No timing or gameplay execution. Internal V8 properties are diagnostic only.

criteria.scope: Development decision for the shared-method game adapter; not device or complete SDK performance acceptance.
criteria.reason: The exploratory result suggests a useful gain in the largest combined case. Require confirmation and no material measured regression before changing the maintained adapter.

prototype.interpretation: Both comparisons improve 18 of 21 medians and the combined 256-actor case by roughly 7–8%; the reversed-startup confirmation exceeds the predeclared 5% slowdown limit for trees at 256 actors (5.1705%). Preserve the prototype for profiling; do not promote it.

preserved.scope: Read-only review identifies concurrent save-and-exit lifecycle/UI/launcher tests and documentation, including replacement of the performance-only preload. The observed main entry also imports an existing bounty passage module. These paths remain owned by game development. No original files or index are written. The frozen extraction capsule is unchanged; no all-file identity claim is made.

limitations: Desktop full-resolver workload includes equal resets and read-only observation costs; not whole-frame or target-device measurement.
Fixed-time warm repeated hits retain coalesced cue rows; cold cue, allocation volume and actor update costs are not isolated.
Original comparisons include preceding SDK/stat-cache changes and cannot isolate sustain performance.
The initial untimed development audit is retained but excluded: helpers changed while it executed; later immutable runs and fault controls provide acceptance.
The initial short timing plan is retained; longer warmup/batches improve measurement quality without changing workload arithmetic.
Full SDK completion, physical Steam Deck/mobile acceptance and remaining native package integration are open.
